The workshop runs over **three full days** (9:00 am – 5:00 pm, one-hour lunch break) in the conference room of **Knight Campus Building 2** at the University of Oregon. An **optional Day 0** runs the previous day on the same schedule for participants who want a refresher on R, the Unix command line, Git, or basic single-cell biology before the workshop proper begins.

::: callout-tip
**Before Day 1:** complete the [Software Setup](Software_Setup.qmd) on the laptop you'll bring. Plan 30–60 minutes, the day before — *not* the morning of.
:::

## Day 0 (optional) — Software Setup & Computational Refresher

For participants who want extra help before the workshop proper. Same hours, same room. **Drop in for the parts you need.**

| Time | Topic | Material |
|---|---|---|
| 9:00 – 10:30 | Laptop setup help — R, RStudio, packages, the workshop dataset | [Software Setup](Software_Setup.qmd) |
| 10:30 – 12:00 | R fundamentals refresher — tidyverse, writing functions | [Appendix D](Resources_Folder/Appendix_D_R_Programming.html) |
| 12:00 – 1:00 | Lunch | — |
| 1:00 – 2:30 | Unix command line — `cd`, `ls`, pipes, `grep`, `wget` | [Appendix B](Resources_Folder/Appendix_B_Unix_Command_Line.html), [Appendix C](Resources_Folder/Appendix_C_GREP_Regex_Shell.html) |
| 2:30 – 3:30 | Git & GitHub basics | [Appendix E](Resources_Folder/Appendix_E_Git_GitHub.html) |
| 3:30 – 5:00 | Single-cell biology refresher + intro to the workshop dataset | [Appendix H](Resources_Folder/Appendix_H_SC_Biology_Refresher.html), [Datasets](Datasets.qmd) |

## Bonus tracks — self-paced after the workshop

The following modules are **not part of the three-day in-person workshop**. They ship alongside the workshop materials for you to work through on your own time once you've finished the core sequence:

- **Lecture 10 + Tutorial 09** — Bulk and single-cell ATAC-seq with Signac
- **Lecture 11 + Tutorial 10** — WGCNA on bulk RNA-seq
- **Lecture 12 + Tutorial 11** — Spatial transcriptomics with Visium
- **Lecture 13 + Tutorial 12** — FAIR principles and data submission
- **[Talapas Advanced track](Tutorials.qmd#talapas-advanced-—-hpc-path-raw-fastq-→-differential-abundance)** — the full pipeline on UO's HPC, starting from raw FASTQs and Cell Ranger

## What to bring

- A laptop with at least **16 GB RAM** and **~10 GB free disk**
- R ≥ 4.4 and RStudio Desktop installed (see [Software Setup](Software_Setup.qmd))
- The workshop dataset downloaded and unpacked (the setup script handles this)
- A power adapter — outlets are limited in the conference room

## During-workshop support

The instructors will be in the room throughout the workshop. For questions outside workshop hours, email is the most reliable channel — see the [About](about.qmd) page.
